_comment: Registry of the numeric constants the RBMK model rests on, with their source. Mission rule 2: nothing is guessed. status is one of: verified (cites a primary source, with sourceUrl + quote), to_verify (a reference value not yet confirmed against a primary source), placeholder (a value with no source at all, allowed only as a FALLBACK that is unused while real data is present). The build gate warns on to_verify and FAILS on any non-fallback placeholder; the self-test additionally requires every verified entry to carry a sourceUrl and a quote.

INSAG-7.title: IAEA Safety Series No. 75-INSAG-7, The Chernobyl Accident: Updating of INSAG-1

NUREG-1250.title: Report on the Accident at the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Station (NUREG-1250), US Nuclear Regulatory Commission, January 1987
NUREG-1250.publisher: US Nuclear Regulatory Commission (with DOE, EPRI, EPA, FEMA, INPO)
NUREG-1250.note: Independent of IAEA/INSAG. Its Table 2.4 (section 2.3.2) is compiled from Soviet primary sources (Dollezhal 1980a, USSR 1986, Romanenko 1982, Virgil'ev 1979). Used here to CORROBORATE the feedback-coefficient signs, not as the value source.

delayed.beta_eff.source: RBMK literature (value commonly quoted for the RBMK-1000). INSAG-7 uses beta_eff as the reactivity unit but does not tabulate its numeric value.
delayed.beta_eff.note: To confirm against a NIKIET/design source. The RBMK used its own six-group delayed-neutron set (see delayed.lambda_i).

delayed.generation_time.note: To confirm against a NIKIET/design source.

delayed.lambda_i.note: The RBMK used its own six-group set — replace from a NIKIET/ABBN source. INSAG-7 Annex II notes the accident analyses used 18 delayed-neutron groups, so a higher-group RBMK set exists.

delayed.beta_fractions.note: RBMK-specific group abundances to be sourced (see delayed.lambda_i).

feedback.void_coeff.source: INSAG-7 Table II-I (p. 105), 'Void coefficient of reactivity at the working point' = +2.0e-4 per % void; +2.0e-4 per 1% = 0.020 per unit void fraction. INSAG-7 sec. 2.1 gives the full range: -1.3e-4 (fresh fuel) to +(2.0-2.5)e-4 per % void (steady-state refuelling).
feedback.void_coeff.quote: Void coefficient of reactivity af at the working point (%-' (5k/k) void) +2.0 x 10"4

feedback.doppler_coeff.source: INSAG-7 Table II-I (p. 105), 'Fuel temperature coefficient of reactivity' = -1.2e-5 per degC.
feedback.doppler_coeff.quote: Fuel temperature coefficient of reactivity aT ("C"1) -1.2 x 10'5

feedback.graphite_coeff.source: CONFLICT WITH PRIMARY SOURCE. The code carries -2.0e-5 (negative). INSAG-7 Table II-I (p. 105) states the graphite temperature coefficient as +6e-5 (POSITIVE), and INSAG-7 sec. 4.7.3 twice calls it 'the positive graphite temperature coefficient of reactivity'. INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED: NUREG-1250 (US NRC, Jan 1987) sec. 2.3.2.2 states 'The graphite temperature coefficient is positive', and its Table 2.4 gives +3.2e-5 (fresh) to +6e-5 (steady-state) per degC, compiled from Soviet primary sources (Dollezhal, Romanenko, Virgil'ev). Two independent agencies agree the sign is positive; the code's negative value has no support.
feedback.graphite_coeff.note: A POSITIVE graphite coefficient is a genuine, documented RBMK destabilising property; a negative value is not. Both INSAG-7 and NUREG-1250 agree the sign is positive. The sign is left as-is here (changing it alters the accident model and the RbmkSpatialSelfTest temperature assertion) pending the Director's decision. RESOLVE by flipping the sign; the only open question is magnitude (3.2e-5 fresh vs 6e-5 equilibrium).
feedback.graphite_coeff.quote: Graphite temperature coefficient of reactivity ac (CC~') 6 x 10~5

feedback.power_coeff.source: Lumped damping term in the model. NOT the INSAG-7 'fast power coefficient' (-0.5e-4 dk/k per MW(th), Table II-I): that is per MW and gives ~-0.16 dk/k at 3200 MW(th), a different quantity in different units. The model's per-unit-power coefficient still needs a source.
feedback.power_coeff.note: Confirm the intended definition (per unit power fraction vs per MW) and source the value.

xenon.coeff.source: Reference value; INSAG-7 does not tabulate a xenon worth.
xenon.coeff.note: To confirm against a NIKIET/design source. (Note: Xenon.java uses a -0.03 equilibrium scale, and ReactorCore/SpatialReactorCore hard-code 0.024 separately — these should be reconciled to one sourced value.)

rodworth.scale.source: Reference worth used to scale the perturbation sum. INSAG-7 Table II-I gives per-rod efficiencies instead: 'Minimum efficiency of RCPS rods 10.5%' and 'Efficiency of manual control rods 7.5%' (of the core's reactivity), plus rod travel speed 0.4 m/s (Annex II).
rodworth.scale.note: Replace with a measured/design rod-worth curve. The INSAG-7 efficiencies (10.5% / 7.5%) are the calibration target.

spatial.void_feedback.unit: dk/k per unit void (measured from the 3D solver)
spatial.void_feedback.source: Measured from RbmkSolver3D: dk/d(void) = +0.105/unit, i.e. ~5x the INSAG-7 value (+0.020/unit). The derived one-node lattice cell overstates the feedback; the calibration the legacy path applied (VOID_FEEDBACK_SCALE) was removed when the derived constants were wired in (commit ebaab1c).
spatial.void_feedback.note: This is why SpatialReactorCoreSelfTest's AZ-5 check ('the core is shut down after AZ-5') FAILS: after a scram the fuel cooldown contributes ~+0.039 dk/k of positive reactivity (Doppler also ~7x strong), cancelling the ~0.038 dk/k rod worth. The spatial feedbacks must be re-anchored to INSAG-7 before the spatial core can be called correct.

xsec.void_feedback_scale.source: Hand-set scale used only by the legacy fallback cell when the derived lattice table is missing. Not used when rbmk_lattice.json is present.

xsec.doppler_feedback_scale.source: Hand-set scale used only by the legacy fallback cell. Not used when the derived lattice table is present.

lattice.library.source: Currently ENDF/B-VIII.0 via the openmc-data-storage JSON mirror. AGREED TARGET: ROSFOND / ABBN-RF (NIKIET lineage). Swap via tools/lattice --source rosfond.
